title: International organisations
examples: What is the main goal of the United Nations?
How is the European Union different from the World Trade Organization?
Can an international organisation make laws for countries?

explain.say: Today we will learn about international organisations. These groups help countries work together. They try to solve big world problems.
The United Nations is a major global body. It aims to promote peace and international cooperation. It has many different committees working on various issues.
The European Union involves many European countries. It aims to create a single market for goods and services. This level of cooperation is very deep.
ASEAN brings together nations in Southeast Asia. Its main focus is economic growth and regional stability. It helps its members cooperate peacefully.
The Commonwealth is a group of nations with historical links. They cooperate on various issues like trade and democracy. Membership is based on shared history.
The World Trade Organization manages global trade rules. It aims to reduce trade barriers between member countries. This keeps trade flowing smoothly.

faq.q: What is the difference between the UN and the EU?
faq.a: The UN is a much broader global body focused on peace and general international law. The EU involves a deeper level of integration, creating a single economic market among its members.
asks: Does the EU have more power than the UN?
What makes the EU different from the UN?

faq.q: Does ASEAN enforce its rules on its members?
faq.a: ASEAN primarily encourages cooperation through consensus among its member states. It relies more on mutual agreement than on strict enforcement mechanisms.
asks: How does ASEAN make countries follow its rules?

faq.q: What is the main purpose of the WTO?
faq.a: The WTO's main purpose is to ensure that international trade happens according to agreed-upon rules. It helps countries negotiate lower tariffs and fewer trade restrictions.

faq.q: Is the Commonwealth a trade group like the WTO?
faq.a: No, the Commonwealth is more focused on shared political values and historical connections. While trade can be discussed, it is not primarily a trade organization.
asks: What kind of group is the Commonwealth?

faq.q: Do all countries have to join these organisations?
faq.a: No, membership is voluntary. Countries choose to join based on their interests and their desire to cooperate with others.
asks: Can a country leave these groups?

facts: The UN was established after the Second World War to maintain global peace.
The EU allows its members to use a single currency in some areas.
The WTO deals with reducing tariffs and trade barriers worldwide.
ASEAN focuses its efforts on political and economic stability in Southeast Asia.

quiz.say: Which organisation focuses on creating a single economic market among its members?
quiz.why: The EU's core goal is deep economic integration, creating a single market for trade.

wrong.1: The UN is broader and focuses more on peace than a single market.
wrong.2: The WTO focuses only on trade rules, not creating a single market.
wrong.3: ASEAN focuses on regional stability, not the deep integration of a single market.

quiz.say: If a country wants to reduce tariffs on goods with many partners, which organisation is most relevant?
quiz.why: The WTO's entire purpose is to govern and reduce trade barriers like tariffs.

wrong.0: The UN deals with peace, not primarily trade tariffs.
wrong.1: The Commonwealth's focus is more on shared political history.
wrong.2: The EU is a specific bloc, not the global forum for all trade rules.

quiz.say: Which organisation is primarily concerned with promoting peace and global cooperation on a massive scale?
quiz.why: The UN's founding mandate is centered on preventing conflict and fostering peace worldwide.

wrong.0: The Commonwealth's focus is historical and political, not global peace enforcement.
wrong.2: ASEAN's focus is limited to the Southeast Asian region.
wrong.3: The WTO's focus is strictly on the rules of international trade.
